raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan for my 350 mu.

---

*I've worked this ground 20 years, my father before me. Never had much schooling but I know what this sandy soil wants. My 350 mu, I split it like always — mostly sweetpotato because that's what does well here and buyers come looking for it. Maize on another chunk, and a bit of millet on the drier ground. Got my wife and two kids at home, but kids are in school most of the year, so I hire plenty of hands come planting and digging time.*

**Sweetpotato, about 200 mu** — This is my main thing. I start planting slips end of April once the soil warms. Old Wang in the next village, I've been buying slips from him ten years, he raises them good. Before planting I hire the tractor fella to run the ridger through. For fertilizer, two bags of the 15-15-15 compound per mu, that's 80 kg, put it in the ridge before the slips go in. My father always said too much of the urea stuff and you get all vines and no tubers — I seen that myself when I tried it as a young man. So just the compound. Maybe I throw in a bit of potash if it's cheap at the shop, helps the tubers fill out.

Planting 200 mu by hand needs hands — I bring in 15-20 village folk for two, three weeks. Same story in October for digging. Can't do it with just family.

Water — depends on the sky. July-August if it gets dry I turn on the well, maybe once or twice. The pump costs money so I wait till the vines start to droop.

Bugs — one spray in midseason for the weevils and leaf eaters, usually enough.

Expect 2800-3000 kg/mu if the weather cooperates. Good year maybe 3200, bad year drops to 2400.

**Maize, 100 mu** — Spring maize since I'm not doing wheat here. Plant end of April through early May. I buy the good hybrid seed from the ag shop, whatever the clerk says is running well that year. One bag compound at planting, then one bag urea when the plants get waist-high at the big-trumpet stage. Water once, maybe twice, if it's a dry summer. Expect around 450 kg/mu, could hit 500 if everything lines up.

**Millet, the remaining 50 mu** — on my drier ground where the well doesn't reach so good. Plant in May. Half a bag of compound per mu and that's it, no topdress. Millet is tough, it takes what you give it. No irrigation. Family can handle most of the work, maybe my wife does the harvest with me. Expect 250 kg/mu. Some for our own kitchen, rest goes to the market.

All up, I'll spend maybe 200,000 yuan on inputs and labor this year. Sweetpotato is where most of it goes and most of it comes back.
